analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: Acute liquidation across Europe and the US: a rolling wave of de-risking across long/short funds spilled into systematic strategies. Losses were widespread in fundamental long/short, TMT, Asian long/short, multi-strat and systematic. Popular longs fell and popular shorts rose.
Unconstrained momentum is suffering its worst drawdown since the GFC, outside COVID. The desk compares it to 2018, with a considerably more extreme scale.

The AI selloff made the least sense of any day in this move, per the EMEA trading head. AI versus SPX ex-AI had its worst relative day since the DeepSeek moment. Bloom Energy fell on cash conversion despite a strong quarter, and WDC fell despite a roughly 20% EPS guidance beat and raise, with some capex concerns.

The desk reads the AI weakness as a repricing of the cost of capital rather than weaker demand. Unlimited cheap capital for the buildout is being challenged, and the options (cut capex, delay deployment, fund with equity) are not supportive of equity prices. Underlying AI demand is described as robust.

Cybersecurity: critical PHP exploits, a serious Java vulnerability and a Python supply chain compromise emerged at once. The desk sees this as bullish for cybersecurity spending because AI lowers the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface grows.

Oil: crude extended its breakout, with front contracts taking out recent highs as geopolitical risk premium widens into the weekend. Outcomes are described as binary: a rapid, targeted engagement could trigger a sell-the-news unwind, while retaliatory disruption at key energy chokepoints would constrain balances.

Rates: AI loses, bonds win. The 10-year yield fell about 15bps, the largest one-day move since August 2025, as the AI selloff forces a reassessment of longer-term growth. Rates have diverged from oil. If energy resolves, the desk questions how much further relief rates get, and if AI stabilizes, rates could come under pressure again.

Dispersion was extreme: the index broke lower on heavyweights while equal weight/RSP closed near session highs, up 68bps. 155 S&P names had moves of 2.0 sigma or more (most since the May 2025 US-China tariff truce), and 335 S&P names rose, one of the widest gaps between breadth and index performance since the 1990s.

Hedge fund performance: as of midday, GS PB showed Fundamental L/S down 1.1%, Systematics down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4%, the first time since Covid all three fell more than 1% on the same day. The GS HF Positioning Pair (GSTHVIPP) finished down about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% month to date.

AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 23% from its June highs, a similar drawdown to the one before the July bounce. High Beta Momentum (GSPRHIMO) has erased all YTD gains. SPX ex-AI (SPXXAI) has outperformed the S&P by 6% month to date.

Flows: no sign of buying the AI theme on the desk. The GS floor finished 9.6% better for sale, asset managers about 20% better for sale (large cap tech and ETFs), and hedge funds 10% better for sale (semis, hardware, and ETF shorting with shorts outpacing long sales 2:1). Floor activity was a 5 out of 10.

Derivatives: the desk describes capitulation and de-grossing. Skew was bid at the open and faded into the close, SPX fixed-strike vols rose almost a vol in gamma tenors before fading, and NDX vols were bid. Clients bought VIX upside, and large-size CRWV upside buying stood out as a contrarian bullish expression among hyperscalers. S&P implied move for the next session is 0.74%.

Catalysts: major hyperscaler results next week are seen as critical, especially backlog conversion to revenue, deployment pace and funding commentary. WDC reported after the close (+2% after hours). The desk expected Korea down another mid-single digits and sees its resilience as encouraging.

sector_views.rationale: AI lowers the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface expands, so security spending should accelerate.
AI-linked names are under pressure from a cost-of-capital repricing and capex funding concerns, though demand is described as robust and momentum drawdowns have historically been attractive entries.

earnings_insights: WDC: roughly 20% EPS guidance beat and raise per the desk, with some incremental capex concerns. Shares fell in the session and were +2% after hours.
Bloom Energy fell overnight over cash conversion despite a blowout quarter.
META and LRCX earnings reactions were not constructive on the day, after constructive reactions on Wednesday. TSLA and IBM also failed to lift the market.
Major hyperscaler results next week are the next catalyst, with focus on backlog conversion, deployment pace and funding.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Largest one-day move since August 2025, driven by the AI selloff lowering growth expectations. The 10-year closed below the CTA short-term threshold, which could bring bond demand in the next morning's flow estimates.
Back to YTD highs on escalating Middle East tensions.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell 387bps to $81,309 in the session.
risk_factors: Funding risk for the AI buildout: cheaper capital assumptions are being challenged, forcing capex cuts, delayed deployment or equity funding.
Binary Middle East escalation risk and oil chokepoint disruption.
Rates and AI reflexivity: relief in either could pressure the other and does not support equities.
Investors worried about gigawatt delivery, too many gigawatts, insufficient capital and insufficient power, with little differentiation across pockets.
vol_and_positioning: Skew went bid at the open and trickled lower into the close. SPX fixed-strike vols rose almost a vol in gamma tenors before fading, with spot closing about midway between the 50-day and 100-day moving averages.
NDX vols were bid on the underperformance, showing where positioning and pain are concentrated.
Clients bought VIX upside and showed defensive posturing. Large-size CRWV upside buying stood out.
S&P implied move through the next session is 0.74%.
GS HF Positioning Pair (GSTHVIPP) down about 4.2%, worst since 2011, and down 10.4% month to date.
Unconstrained momentum is in its worst drawdown since the GFC outside COVID.
The S&P had a $6.2bn market-on-close buy imbalance. 18.711bn shares traded versus a YTD daily average of 18.535bn.
geopolitical: Escalating Middle East tensions with precautionary diplomatic posture changes in the Gulf and heightened regional security alerts, pushing oil to year-to-date highs.
Post-midterm political implications cited as a reason investors will not add risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Underlying AI demand remains robust and frontier model development is strong, with further advances expected. Momentum drawdowns of this kind have historically been attractive entry points and hyperscaler results next week could stabilize the tape.
tension_points.bear_case: Cheap capital for the buildout is being challenged, forcing capex cuts, delayed deployment or equity funding, and the desk notes none of these support equity prices. Floor flow showed no buying of the AI theme.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler results next week showing weak backlog conversion, slower deployment or heavier equity funding.

tension_points.bull_case: Crude has broken out and front contracts took out recent highs. Any retaliatory disruption across key chokepoints would leave global balances severely constrained.
tension_points.bear_case: A rapid, targeted engagement with no secondary infrastructure damage could trigger an immediate sell-the-news unwind, and the desk feels the elevated risk is already a lot in the price.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A targeted engagement with no secondary infrastructure damage would unwind the premium.
